external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A shopper who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party card processor that settles payments and sends payment-status webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run through which shoppers browse and place orders.
processes.source_excerpt: a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.technology: Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that processes orders and writes receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four data.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts that record which order was written and that the order service wrote it.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A shopper signs in to the storefront using email and password and receives a session cookie.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: A shopper places an order through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four in the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for every completed order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket
data_flows.authentication: the order service's own service account
data_flows.data_description: receipt recording which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor posts a webhook to tell the storefront API that an order is paid.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source states: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."
data_flows.data_description: payment settlement status and order-paid notification

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The internet-facing zone from which shoppers reach the storefront API.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The internal network containing the order service and the order-capture data stores.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: third party
trust_boundaries.description: A zone controlled by an external party, including the card processor.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is called an API and receives a POST webhook; this supports treating its caller-facing interface as web.

assumptions.assumption: orders-db is in the core network zone.
assumptions.basis: The database is used by the order service, which the source explicitly places in the core network; the source does not name a separate zone for orders-db.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive is in the core network zone.
assumptions.basis: The receipt archive is the order service's destination and the source names no separate zone for the bucket.
The source states that it contains shopper addresses and card-last-four data.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that it contains order receipts and identifies completed orders.
